![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/49b119b378ac4f45c0c395ca77c5cefead3a7c811295b51ac8eaa8aef7100e25.png)

The base of a solid is the region enclosed by the curves $y=1-{x}^{2}$ and $y=-1,$  as shown in the picture. Cross-sections perpendicular to the $x$-axis are rectangles. If the height of each rectangle is $2$ times the length of its base, which integral gives the volume of the solid?
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=1-{x}^{2}$ and $g(x)=-1.$

First, we determine the limits of integration. To do that, we find the intersections of the two curves by setting the functions equal to one another and solving for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 1-{x}^{2} & =-1 \\ {x}^{2} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the limit of integration are $x=-\sqrt{2}$ and $x=\sqrt{2}.$

Now, consider a cross-section at some point $x$, where $x\in (-\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2})$,  and its projection on the $xy$-plane: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/0c2a676ecc781a2a7a78870eb93ee9fbe5a89a7bd754a446231c6e3237f75831.png)

The base of the cross-section is

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =|f(x)-g(x)| \\  & =|1-{x}^{2}-(-1)| \\  & =|2-{x}^{2}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of a rectangle is
$A=bh.$
  So, since we have $h=2b,$ the expression for the area of the cross-section is

$$
\begin{aligned}A(x) & =bh \\  & =2{b}^{2} \\  & =2{(2-{x}^{2})}^{2} \\  & =8-8{x}^{2}+2{x}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now calculate the volume of the solid, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={\int }_{c}^{d}A(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{2}}(8-8{x}^{2}+2{x}^{4})\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
